specification.problem: Given a 4-bit reversible function as a permutation pi of {0..15}, find a cascade of NOT/CNOT/Toffoli (optionally Peres, Fredkin) gates on 4 wires realizing pi with minimum quantum cost QC (sum of gate costs), then realize it as a 4-qubit circuit and verify it reproduces pi.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny explicit instance: 4 wires, NCT library with optional Peres/Fredkin, exact minimum-QC synthesis by meet-in-the-middle over permutations, then Qiskit realization and basis-state verification of all 16 inputs. Not covered: the paper's actual gate-count-optimal tool internals, equivalence-class symmetry reduction details, benchmark list, and the reported savings of up to 74%.

symbols.meaning: target reversible function as a permutation
i-th gate of the network, as a permutation of {0..15}
total quantum cost of a network
hash table of permutations reachable with cost at most j
basis input on wires (a,b,c,d); in Qiskit, a is qubit 0 (little-endian integer x=a+2b+4c+8d)

equations.label: Network realizes target
equations.description: A cascade of gates composes to the target permutation.
equations.justification: Standard model of reversible circuits as permutations; chosen for the specification.

equations.label: Quantum cost as sum of gate costs
equations.latex: QC=\sum_{i=1}^m c(g_i),\quad c(\mathrm{NOT})=c(\mathrm{CNOT})=1,\ c(\mathrm{Toffoli})=5,\ c(\mathrm{Peres})=4,\ c(\mathrm{Fredkin})=7
equations.justification: Standard quantum cost values recalled from the literature; the abstract only names quantum cost.

equations.label: Optimal cost objective
equations.latex: QC^*(\pi)=\min\{\sum_i c(g_i):\ g_m\circ\cdots\circ g_1=\pi,\ g_i\in L\}
equations.description: Exact minimization of quantum cost over networks in library L.
equations.abstract_quote: exact minimization of quantum cost (QC) in 4-bit circuits
equations.justification: The abstract states the goal of exact QC minimization; the formula is the natural formalization.
assumptions: L = NCT, optionally with Peres and Fredkin

equations.label: Meet-in-the-middle match
equations.latex: QC^*(\pi)=\min_{\sigma\in H_{\lceil k/2\rceil},\ \tau\in H_{\lfloor k/2\rfloor},\ \tau\circ\sigma=\pi}\big(QC(\sigma)+QC(\tau)\big),\quad \text{equivalently } \tau^{-1}\circ\pi=\sigma\ \text{is looked up in }H
equations.description: For each stored tau, test whether tau^{-1} composed with pi lies in the hash table; the minimum over k gives the exact optimum.
equations.justification: The meet-in-the-middle search comes from the sketch, not the abstract. Splitting by cost across gate boundaries needs care, since a gate's cost may straddle the midpoint.
assumptions: Gate set closed under inversion (true for NCT, Peres inverse may need to be added)

equations.label: Relative saving
equations.description: Percentage saving relative to a previously known circuit.
equations.abstract_quote: savings in QC of up to 74% comparing with previously known circuits
equations.justification: The abstract reports percent savings; the formula is the usual definition.

registers.name: q[0..3]
registers.role: data wires a,b,c,d; qubit 0 = a (least significant bit); no ancillas

specification.initial_state: Computational basis state |x> for each x in {0..15}, run one at a time, or the unitary is read directly.

steps.description: Define the gate library with costs and each gate as a permutation of 16 values.
BFS over cost levels (Dijkstra by cost) to build hash tables of permutations reachable at cost up to k/2, optionally reduced by wire-permutation and inversion symmetry.
For increasing k, match the target against products with stored permutations to find the minimal-cost decomposition.
Build the network in Qiskit using x, cx, ccx; Peres as ccx then cx; verify that the unitary or basis mapping equals pi.
Compute QC as the sum of costs and the percent saving versus the reference circuit.

specification.measurement: None for unitary check; alternatively read the statevector for each basis input and compare the output index to pi(x).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute QC of the found network, compare with the known circuit's QC, and report the percent saving.
assumptions: Standard NCV costs NOT/CNOT=1, Toffoli=5, Peres=4, Fredkin=7
Exact gate-count-optimal 4-variable synthesizer can be reused or extended for QC
Gate library is NCT, possibly with Peres and Fredkin
Qiskit realization uses ccx; the 5-primitive NCV decomposition is for costing only
